correctness.rationale: Every automorphism is a weighted cycle rotation because independent natural basis squares force disjoint supports. The explicit recurrence gives c_0^(2^n-1)=t^(1-2^s); cyclic-group power maps count A_s. Cycle products of the resulting monomial action equal c_0^H_s t^J_s; the equality-to-one condition counts B_s and controls the fixed dimension 0 or gcd(n,s). Burnside gives all-tuple orbits. At q=43,n=6,t=37, the shifts 0,2,4 produce precisely 63 automorphisms, only the identity fixes a nonzero vector; conjugation on diagonal C21 acts by exponent 16, proving noncommutativity. Independently constructed finite-field automorphism matrices and Gaussian elimination reproduce the claimed polynomial in 843 configurations including extension fields. Finite experiments corroborate but are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The two distinct root-of-unity obstructions quantify both rational rotation liftability and fixed-linear-space behavior in a natural infinite family of simple, perfect nonassociative algebras. The uniform enumerator determines every finite-field automorphism fixed-vector multiplicity and every tuple-orbit number. A concrete nonabelian 63-element group acting freely on the nonzero vectors of a six-dimensional simple evolution algebra is a structurally motivated, nontrivial realization; its relevance does not depend on claiming first realization among all algebras.
